The first pathway involves Biperiden binding to Chrm2, which is subsequently bound by Trospium, leading to the inhibition of Cyp2d6. This suggests a direct enzymatic interaction through the trospium–Cyp2d6 axis. The second pathway, involving Biperiden's resemblance to Cloperastine and Triprolidine, highlights a structural similarity that may facilitate similar binding interactions, ultimately leading to Cyp2d6 inhibition. Both pathways share a common ancestor in the class of organonitrogen heterocyclic compounds and histamine-1 receptor antagonists, reinforcing the biological relevance of the observed interactions. The integrated evidence suggests that Biperiden may modulate Cyp2d6 through a mechanism involving receptor binding and subsequent enzymatic inhibition, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
